name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,526

clue.text: One taking the law into his own hands leaving IT in disarray

definitions.text: One taking the law into his own hands

indicators.note: things in disarray are jumbled out of order, so the letters before it must be rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: A rogue enforcer storms out, leaving the IT department in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante is a private citizen who punishes suspected wrongdoers without legal authority.

clue.text: Servant's farewell to Turkish leader

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the word before it is kept

blocks.note: vale is a Latin word for goodbye used in English
the initial letter of Turkish

explanation.surface: A servant bids goodbye to the head of the Turkish state.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a manservant who looks after his employer's clothes and personal needs.

clue.text: Relative given most of out-of-date American breakfast dish

indicators.note: most of something means nearly all of it, so the final letter of the following word is dropped

blocks.note: a grandmother is a relative
something out of date is old
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Grandma gets most of a stale American breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Granola is a baked mix of oats, nuts and honey eaten in the morning with milk or yoghurt.

clue.text: Permission to depart

blocks.note: first meaning: authorisation
second meaning: the verb to go away

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase, permission to go, but it splits into a noun and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means authorised absence; as a verb it means go away from a place.

clue.text: Regular tuna cooked with rocket and leeks for starters

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new order
starters are what come first, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: taken as written
initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A recipe: ordinary tuna cooked with rocket and leeks.
explanation.walkthrough: Don't forget the little word 'and': its first letter supplies the second A.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural and regular both describe something normal, as expected, not artificial or unusual.

clue.text: Set arranged by setter's qualified to be respected

indicators.note: arranged suggests putting things into a new order, so the preceding word's letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
the setter is 'I', and setter's stands for 'I am'
qualified means capable

explanation.surface: Something the crossword setter arranged earns respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimable means worthy of esteem, so someone estimable is a person deserving admiration.

clue.text: Advance payments for vehicles

blocks.note: first meaning: advances on wages, a British informal usage
second meaning: short for submarines, underwater craft

explanation.surface: Paying a deposit up front on some cars.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a sub is a loan against future wages; it is also the shortened name of an underwater boat.

clue.text: Special stick for 12?

definitions.note: a cross-reference to 12 across, whose answer is SPLASH, used here as a noun

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
to lodge is to become stuck fast

explanation.surface: A special adhesive to fix something mentioned elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Look up 12 across to find the definition; a splodge is a dollop of colour, much like a splash.
explanation.definitionFit: A splodge and a splash are both irregular smears or patches of liquid or paint.

clue.text: Device for tracking criminal placed under faulty U-bends in German parliament building

definitions.note: strictly the Bundestag is the assembly, which sits in the Reichstag building

indicators.note: something faulty is broken, so the letters following are disordered
in a down entry, being under means this piece follows the earlier one

blocks.note: letters taken as printed, hyphen ignored
an electronic tag is fitted to offenders to monitor them

explanation.surface: A tracking device for an offender is hidden under broken plumbing in the Berlin parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bundestag is Germany's federal parliament, the lower chamber elected by the people.

clue.text: Nice plants woven round centre of wreath

indicators.note: weaving interlaces strands, so the letters are mixed together anew
going round something means surrounding it, placing one piece inside another
the centre is the middle, so only the middle letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the two central letters of this six-letter word

explanation.surface: Pretty greenery woven into a wreath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the adjective meaning agreeable, not the French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and pleasant are synonyms meaning agreeable, enjoyable or likeable.

clue.text: Clever folk put fermented liquid into explosive

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: trinitrotoluene, the familiar explosive
ale is beer made by fermentation

explanation.surface: Bright sparks spike a bomb with home brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent can mean gifted people collectively, as in a club scouting for young players with ability.

clue.text: Pet to beat?

blocks.note: first meaning: to caress an animal gently
second meaning: a blow or hit

explanation.surface: Whether to stroke or smack a household animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a noun, an animal, but it is a verb meaning caress.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a gentle caress with the hand and a single blow struck at something.

clue.text: Setter consumed by strange desire for drugs?

indicators.note: something consumed is taken inside, so it sits within the other piece
strange suggests oddly altered, so the following word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself as me
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to an odd craving for narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is mild: medicines rather than illicit drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedies are medicines or treatments, so drugs in the medical sense are a fair example.

clue.text: Part of window housing edges of principal display

indicators.note: housing something means holding it inside, so one piece contains the other
edges are the outer extremes, so only the first and last letters are taken

blocks.note: a sash is the sliding frame in a window
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A window frame holding the main exhibit.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a prominent display, as in making a splash or a front-page splash in a newspaper.

clue.text: Spread timber supporting roof of mine over stone

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so the first piece comes before the second

blocks.note: a pit prop holds up the roof of a mine shaft
agate is a banded semi-precious stone

explanation.surface: Mining instructions: brace the ceiling with beams resting on rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roof of mine' tempts you to take M, but it belongs to the description of the timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate is to spread or disseminate, as with ideas, or to breed plants.

clue.text: Spooky time in room over water at the beginning of November

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is the only one kept

blocks.note: a hall is a room
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
informal word for urine
initial letter

explanation.surface: A haunted room with water at the start of November, around the time of ghosts.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled; scorecards abbreviate it O.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween, 31 October, is the night associated with ghosts, witches and costumes, hence a spooky date.

clue.text: Brief sign next to note about excessive text for musicians

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the last letter of the following word is lost
turning about means facing the other way, so the next word reads backwards

blocks.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
a musical note
OTT, over the top, is British slang for excessive

explanation.surface: A sign-writer's note complains about overly long text for a band.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT stands for over the top, an everyday British abbreviation meaning excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the written words of an opera or musical, sung by the performers.

clue.text: Animal swallowing large seal swimming to get plant-based food

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so the following pieces go within the first
swimming suggests moving about freely, so the letters drift into a new order

blocks.note: a cow is an animal
standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A creature gulps down a big swimming seal to get vegan grub.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage and carrot, so it is made from vegetables.

clue.text: English language holding daughter back

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
the old Scandinavian language
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: The English tongue keeping a girl at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a direction word for reversal, but it is the definition, meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or plan is to support or approve it publicly.

clue.text: Punish favourite dog

blocks.note: to whip is to punish by lashing
the teacher's pet is the favourite

explanation.surface: Punishing a favourite hound.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippet is a slender racing breed of dog resembling a small greyhound.

clue.text: Come out of space with short green bananas

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the next word loses its last letter
bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

blocks.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sprouting from the ground with unripe fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit to go with green, but it is the slang word for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view from somewhere hidden or enclosed.

clue.text: Select raft to carry mythological princess

indicators.note: the words carry the answer within them, so it is concealed inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Choosing a boat to transport a princess from legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is the Greek heroine, daughter of King Agamemnon, who avenged her father's murder.

clue.text: Brown cross over source of Indian dish

indicators.note: turning over flips something, so the preceding word reads from end to start
a source is where something begins, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: tan is a light brown
a rood is a crucifix
initial letter

explanation.surface: An angry, sunburnt diner, upset over the origin of a curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian dish' looks like the definition, but Indian supplies a letter, leaving just 'dish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori is a style of food cooked in a clay oven, so a tandoori is a dish.

clue.text: Stop claiming runs where batsman stands

indicators.note: claiming something means taking it in, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: to cease is to stop
the cricket scorer's abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire halts play over disputed runs at the batting end.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is a white line marked at each end of the pitch where the batsman takes guard.
explanation.definitionFit: The batting crease is the marked line in front of the stumps behind which a batter is safe.

clue.text: Fabric in garment covering end of zipper

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it, so one piece goes inside another
the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak
final letter

explanation.surface: Cloth in a coat that hides the bottom of the zip.
explanation.definitionFit: Crape is a variant of crepe, a thin crinkled cloth once worn for mourning.

clue.text: Small dish containing large plug

indicators.note: containing something means holding it inside, so a piece sits within another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as in clothing sizes
a pie is a dish
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A modest plate holding a big bung.
explanation.definitionFit: A spile is a small wooden peg or spigot used to stop the hole in a cask.

clue.text: Spiritual lessons taken by poor author

indicators.note: something taken by another is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: bare means meagre, poorly furnished
RI is religious instruction, the school subject

explanation.surface: A struggling writer attends classes in religion.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, is the old British name for school religion classes.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie was the Scottish writer who created Peter Pan.

clue.text: Insect tucked into ordinary banana

indicators.note: something tucked into another is placed inside it

blocks.note: plain means ordinary
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug burrowed into an everyday piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a starchy variety of banana, usually cooked before eating.

clue.text: Time meant to restrict online phenomenon

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the answer is held within the run of words

blocks.note: the letters span the two words

explanation.surface: Time spent trying to limit some internet craze.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is a joke image or idea that spreads virally across the internet.

clue.text: Celebrity entertaining old time revolutionary in Parisian landmark

indicators.note: entertaining guests means having them in, so the following pieces go inside

blocks.note: a big name is a celebrity
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
red is a common label for a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A star hosts a veteran rebel at a famous Paris sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité in the French capital.
